raw_response:
I farm only 3 mu, so I will keep the usual wheat-maize rotation on all of it because that is the system I know best and it fits my land and irrigation. I have farmed a long time, so I do not want to take risks with unfamiliar seed or complicated management. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put on enough nitrogen for steady growth, add phosphorus and potassium as base fertilizer, irrigate a few key times from my well, and keep pesticide use limited to the main disease and insect periods. After wheat harvest, I will quickly prepare the land again and plant maize on the same 3 mu. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I care about stable yield, keep fertilizer at a moderate level, irrigate at the important stages if water is needed, and spray only when pressure is clear. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for my small farm and easier for me to manage at my age.
